title: PGS 11 Final Stage Day 2 is LIVE!!
author: JBowlerr
contents: [p]Hello, PUBG Esports fans![/p][p align="start"]The final stretch of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is approaching: [b]PGS Circuit 4[/b]. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the three remaining tournaments will bring this year’s 12-event PUBG Global Series to a close.[/p][p align="start"]Circuit 4 is more than just the final circuit of the season. With the conclusion of PGS 12, the [b]final PGS Points standings for the 2026 season will be determined, deciding the eight teams that will advance to PUBG Global Championship 2026.[/b][/p][p align="start"]After three circuits of competition, the race for PGC is beginning to take shape—but nothing has been decided yet. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and double points on the line at PGS 12, there are still [b]240 PGS Points[/b] up for grabs.[/p][p align="start"]Which teams will earn their way to PGC 2026 through PGS Points? Let’s take a closer look at [b]Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.[/b][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/QYvMFGPC.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS Circuit 4 Schedule[/b][/h2][p align="start"]PGS Circuit 4 will take place from [b]October 14 to November 1[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]PGS 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Group Stage: October 14[/p][/*][*][p]Winners Stage: October 15[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 16[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 17–18[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 11[/b][/p][list][*][p]Winners Stage: October 22[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 23[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 24–25[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 12[/b][/p][list][*][p]Survival Stage: October 29[/p][/*][*][p]Grand Finals: October 30–November 1[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p align="start"]As the [b]Circuit Final[/b], PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.[/p][p align="start"]When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the [b]2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.[/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/dfU4pJIb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b] [/p][h2][b]PGS Points Standings[/b][/h2][p align="start"]With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.[/p][p align="start"]At the conclusion of Circuit 3, [b]Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points[/b], followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.[/p][p align="start"]Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is [b]Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.[/p][p align="start"]Most importantly, [b]Circuit 4 is still to come.[/b] The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/WQDtO1dg.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The [b]top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings[/b], accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the [b]later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.[/b][/p][p align="start"]The team finishing [b]1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals[/b]. The [b]2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1[/b], while the teams finishing [b]3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage[/b].[/p][p align="start"]This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs[/b][/p][p align="start"]In both [b]PGS 10 and PGS 11[/b], the winner will earn [b]60 PGS Points[/b], with points awarded down through 16th place.[/p][p align="start"]At the Circuit Final, [b]PGS 12, the points will be doubled[/b]. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.[/p][p align="start"]That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:[/p][p align="start"][b]60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.[/p][p align="start"]For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261012/lwSlSIQk.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS 10 Groups[/b][/h2][p align="start"]And it all begins with [b]PGS 10[/b].[/p][p align="start"]The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a [b]snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.[/b][/p][p align="start"]PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.[/p][list][*][p][b]Group A:[/b] Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group B:[/b] T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group C:[/b] Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p align="start"][b]\[Updated: October 12][/b][/p][p align="start"]Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.[/p][p align="start"][i]※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][/*][/list][h2][b]The Final Step to PGC[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.[/p][p align="start"]There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, [b]a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the [b]PGC Grand Finals[/b]?[/p][p align="start"]The final competition of the [b]2026 PUBG Global Series[/b] is about to begin.[/p][p align="start"][b]Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026![/b][/p]

title: PGS 10: The Predator, Virtus.pro
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261022/zDWndffP.jpg" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: calc(100% - 10px); position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; vertical-align: bottom; text-align: center;"][/img][/p][p]Until last year, it felt like the era of Twisted Minds. But this year, everything has changed. The arrival of a predator capable of devouring every team in its path has reshaped the PUBG Esports landscape. And that predator emerged not from Asia or APAC, but from Europe. Its name is Virtus.Pro[b] (VP)[/b], the new dominant force in PUBG Esports.[/p][p]​Of course, VP was not yet the finished product in 2025. The team finished as runners-up at PGS 9 and went on to claim the PGS 10 title. However, when it mattered most at PGC 2025, VP once again had to settle for second place. But the VP of 2026 is a different beast. Starting with a championship victory at PGS 3, VP followed up with a runner-up finish at PEC Spring, third place at PGS 5, and a championship title at the Esports World Cup (EWC). The team then secured back-to-back runner-up finishes at PGS 7 and PGS 8, followed by another second-place finish at PEC Fall. And last week, VP claimed yet another championship at PGS 10. VP now holds a commanding lead in the PGS Points standings and has consistently placed among the top teams at major tournaments throughout the year. So, what exactly has made VP so strong?[b]
[img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261022/uYiR8p58.jpg" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: calc(100% - 10px); position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; vertical-align: bottom; text-align: center;"][/img][/b][/p][p]VP’s biggest transformation began in mid-2025. After announcing his retirement as a professional player, ibiza transitioned into a coaching role with VP, while curexi joined the roster to fill the vacant position. Having made his professional debut in 2018, ibiza competed until 2025 and established himself as one of Europe’s most experienced veterans. He had served as VP’s in-game leader (IGL), but decided to take on a new challenge as a coach to help the team reach the next level.[/p][p]​To fill the gap, VP brought in curexi, who had previously played for prominent organizations such as Heroic and FaZe Clan, strengthening the team’s overall balance. As a coach, ibiza began applying the experience and strategic knowledge he had accumulated over his long career, providing tailored preparation for each tournament. Meanwhile, curexi quickly adapted to the existing roster, requiring little time to find his place within the team.[/p][p]​So, what makes this team so formidable? VP has many strengths, but three stand out in particular.[b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261022/ZlUNqPhv.jpg" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: calc(100% - 10px); position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; vertical-align: bottom; text-align: center;"][/img][/b][/p][p]The first is VP’s ability to make quick, accurate decisions under pressure. Lukarux, the team’s IGL, excels at identifying which positions to secure and which routes to take. Even when circumstances change in an instant, he remains composed and makes decisive calls. Whether attacking or defending, his decisions consistently demonstrate remarkable precision and stability. But these decisions do not come from Lukarux alone. In today’s competitive environment, every player must be capable of making independent decisions. At the same time, those individual decisions must align with the team’s overall strategy. Lukarux establishes the bigger picture, while the other three players make real-time adjustments and contribute the finer details needed to execute that strategy.[/p][p]​As we will explore further, VP’s confidence in its fighting ability—and its understanding of which engagements it can win—forms the foundation of its decision-making. This is why VP often takes a far more aggressive approach than other teams. Once VP identifies a target, the team commits its full attention to it. Teams that fall behind in championship races sometimes struggle because they consider too many options at once, losing sight of what matters most at critical moments. VP is different. The team knows exactly what to prioritize when it matters, and more importantly, how to execute the actions required to achieve its objective.[b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261022/HPnI3PFZ.png" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: calc(100% - 10px); position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; vertical-align: bottom; text-align: center;"][/img][/b][/p][p align="start"]​The second strength is VP’s exceptional fighting ability and technical skill. And to explain this, we have to talk about NIXZYEE. If I had to choose just one player with the most formidable fighting ability in 2026, I would pick NIXZYEE without hesitation. He possesses an extraordinary range of combat techniques and movement skills, combining devastating firepower with excellent teamwork.[/p][p]​His precision when spraying with magnified scopes is almost mechanical. His peeks are astonishingly fast, and his unpredictable movement constantly disrupts his opponents’ timing. With his overwhelming individual skill, NIXZYEE turns every engagement into a nightmare for his opponents. Among all active players, it would not be an exaggeration to call him one of the most complete players in the game. What makes him even more frightening is his constant pursuit of improvement. He continues to study new techniques, refine them, and incorporate them into his gameplay.[/p][p]​But NIXZYEE is far from VP’s only threat. Beami and curexi also bring tremendous firepower to long-range engagements, consistently delivering strong performances. They are particularly dangerous when using sniper rifles (SRs), often securing the first knock against an opponent and creating new opportunities for their team to push forward. Their headshot accuracy is especially impressive. While many professional players maintain headshot rates of around 20%, VP’s players frequently exceed 30%. These precise headshots allow them to knock opponents out of position and create opportunities to take control of areas held by enemy teams. These strengths were on full display at PGS 10. Throughout the tournament, VP recorded 55 first knocks, averaging 5.5 per match.[b]
[img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261022/uDD5ZcV0.png" style="border-style: none; cursor: pointer; padding: 0px 1px; user-select: none; max-width: calc(100% - 10px); position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; vertical-align: bottom; text-align: center;"][/img][/b][/p][p]VP’s third major strength is its ability to build and execute strategies specifically designed to win championships. Its tactical flexibility goes beyond making adjustments within individual matches. VP also analyzes the overall standings, identifies its closest championship rivals, and develops strategies to directly challenge them when necessary. The final match of PGS 10 on Taego is a perfect example.[/p][p]​At the time, VP was tied on 86 points with tournament leader Team Liquid (TL). Rather than simply following its usual strategy and trying to outscore its rival through conventional play, VP made a bold decision. It chose to directly target TL. This was not a reckless gamble. It was a calculated decision based on VP’s confidence in early-game engagements and its analysis of how TL was likely to respond. And the strategy worked almost immediately. VP eliminated two TL players in an early engagement, gaining a decisive advantage from the start. From there, VP systematically shut down the routes TL could use to move into the playable area, limiting its opportunities to recover and earn additional points. By neutralizing its closest rival, VP took control of the championship race. In the end, the title belonged to VP.[/p][p]​[b]Looking Ahead[/b][/p][p]There is still much more to explore when it comes to VP’s winning formula. But with even greater challenges waiting ahead, it would be a shame to reveal every aspect of their strategy just yet.[/p][p]​The predator of 2026 has already conquered PGS. Can VP go one step further and finally lift the PGC trophy it has been chasing? We’ll be watching closely as the predator prepares for its next hunt.[/p][p]​- Jisooboy[/p]

title: PGS 11 Winners Stage is LIVE!!
author: JBowlerr
contents: [p]Hello, PUBG Esports fans![/p][p align="start"]The final stretch of the 2026 PUBG Global Series is approaching: [b]PGS Circuit 4[/b]. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and the Circuit Final, PGS 12, the three remaining tournaments will bring this year’s 12-event PUBG Global Series to a close.[/p][p align="start"]Circuit 4 is more than just the final circuit of the season. With the conclusion of PGS 12, the [b]final PGS Points standings for the 2026 season will be determined, deciding the eight teams that will advance to PUBG Global Championship 2026.[/b][/p][p align="start"]After three circuits of competition, the race for PGC is beginning to take shape—but nothing has been decided yet. With PGS 10, PGS 11, and double points on the line at PGS 12, there are still [b]240 PGS Points[/b] up for grabs.[/p][p align="start"]Which teams will earn their way to PGC 2026 through PGS Points? Let’s take a closer look at [b]Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.[/b][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/QYvMFGPC.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS Circuit 4 Schedule[/b][/h2][p align="start"]PGS Circuit 4 will take place from [b]October 14 to November 1[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]PGS 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Group Stage: October 14[/p][/*][*][p]Winners Stage: October 15[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 16[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 17–18[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 11[/b][/p][list][*][p]Winners Stage: October 22[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 23[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 24–25[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 12[/b][/p][list][*][p]Survival Stage: October 29[/p][/*][*][p]Grand Finals: October 30–November 1[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p align="start"]As the [b]Circuit Final[/b], PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.[/p][p align="start"]When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the [b]2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.[/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/dfU4pJIb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b] [/p][h2][b]PGS Points Standings[/b][/h2][p align="start"]With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.[/p][p align="start"]At the conclusion of Circuit 3, [b]Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points[/b], followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.[/p][p align="start"]Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is [b]Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.[/p][p align="start"]Most importantly, [b]Circuit 4 is still to come.[/b] The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/WQDtO1dg.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The [b]top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings[/b], accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the [b]later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.[/b][/p][p align="start"]The team finishing [b]1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals[/b]. The [b]2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1[/b], while the teams finishing [b]3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage[/b].[/p][p align="start"]This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs[/b][/p][p align="start"]In both [b]PGS 10 and PGS 11[/b], the winner will earn [b]60 PGS Points[/b], with points awarded down through 16th place.[/p][p align="start"]At the Circuit Final, [b]PGS 12, the points will be doubled[/b]. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.[/p][p align="start"]That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:[/p][p align="start"][b]60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.[/p][p align="start"]For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261012/lwSlSIQk.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS 10 Groups[/b][/h2][p align="start"]And it all begins with [b]PGS 10[/b].[/p][p align="start"]The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a [b]snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.[/b][/p][p align="start"]PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.[/p][list][*][p][b]Group A:[/b] Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group B:[/b] T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group C:[/b] Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p align="start"][b]\[Updated: October 12][/b][/p][p align="start"]Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.[/p][p align="start"][i]※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][/*][/list][h2][b]The Final Step to PGC[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.[/p][p align="start"]There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, [b]a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the [b]PGC Grand Finals[/b]?[/p][p align="start"]The final competition of the [b]2026 PUBG Global Series[/b] is about to begin.[/p][p align="start"][b]Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026![/b][/p]

The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.[/p][p align="start"]When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the [b]2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.[/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/dfU4pJIb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b] [/p][h2][b]PGS Points Standings[/b][/h2][p align="start"]With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.[/p][p align="start"]At the conclusion of Circuit 3, [b]Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points[/b], followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.[/p][p align="start"]Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is [b]Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.[/p][p align="start"]Most importantly, [b]Circuit 4 is still to come.[/b] The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/WQDtO1dg.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The [b]top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings[/b], accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the [b]later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.[/b][/p][p align="start"]The team finishing [b]1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals[/b]. The [b]2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1[/b], while the teams finishing [b]3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage[/b].[/p][p align="start"]This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs[/b][/p][p align="start"]In both [b]PGS 10 and PGS 11[/b], the winner will earn [b]60 PGS Points[/b], with points awarded down through 16th place.[/p][p align="start"]At the Circuit Final, [b]PGS 12, the points will be doubled[/b]. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.[/p][p align="start"]That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:[/p][p align="start"][b]60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.[/p][p align="start"]For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261012/lwSlSIQk.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS 10 Groups[/b][/h2][p align="start"]And it all begins with [b]PGS 10[/b].[/p][p align="start"]The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a [b]snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.[/b][/p][p align="start"]PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.[/p][list][*][p][b]Group A:[/b] Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group B:[/b] T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group C:[/b] Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p align="start"][b]\[Updated: October 12][/b][/p][p align="start"]Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.[/p][p align="start"][i]※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][/*][/list][h2][b]The Final Step to PGC[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.[/p][p align="start"]There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, [b]a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the [b]PGC Grand Finals[/b]?[/p][p align="start"]The final competition of the [b]2026 PUBG Global Series[/b] is about to begin.[/p][p align="start"][b]Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026![/b][/p]

Let’s take a closer look at [b]Circuit 4, the final competition of the 2026 PGS season.[/b][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/QYvMFGPC.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS Circuit 4 Schedule[/b][/h2][p align="start"]PGS Circuit 4 will take place from [b]October 14 to November 1[/b].[/p][list][*][p][b]PGS 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Group Stage: October 14[/p][/*][*][p]Winners Stage: October 15[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 16[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 17–18[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 11[/b][/p][list][*][p]Winners Stage: October 22[/p][/*][*][p]Survival Stage: October 23[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage: October 24–25[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]PGS 12[/b][/p][list][*][p]Survival Stage: October 29[/p][/*][*][p]Grand Finals: October 30–November 1[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p align="start"]As the [b]Circuit Final[/b], PGS 12 will see the top eight teams in the Circuit 4 PGS Points standings advance directly to the Grand Finals based on the points accumulated through PGS 10 and PGS 11. The remaining 16 teams will compete in the Survival Stage for the remaining spots in the Grand Finals.[/p][p align="start"]When PGS 12 comes to an end, it will mark not only the conclusion of Circuit 4, but also the end of the [b]2026 season-long PGS Points race spanning PGS 1 through PGS 12.[/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/dfU4pJIb.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/b] [/p][h2][b]PGS Points Standings[/b][/h2][p align="start"]With three circuits and nine PGS events now complete, the battle for PGS Points is more intense than ever.[/p][p align="start"]At the conclusion of Circuit 3, [b]Virtus.pro leads the standings with 261 points[/b], followed by Made in Thailand with 224 points, 17Gaming with 223 points, and T1 with 208 points.[/p][p align="start"]Currently occupying the final PGC qualification spot is [b]Petrichor Road in eighth place with 152 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]But the gaps around the cutoff remain narrow. Seventh-place Falcons sit just two points ahead at 154, while ninth-place Gen.G Esports trail the current PGC qualification line by only seven points with 145.[/p][p align="start"]Most importantly, [b]Circuit 4 is still to come.[/b] The current standings are far from the final picture of who will advance to PGC.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/WQDtO1dg.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGC 2026 Qualification & PGS Points[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The [b]top eight teams in the final PGS Points standings[/b], accumulated across PGS 1 through PGS 12 during the 2026 season, will qualify for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]And the final standings determine more than just qualification. The higher a team finishes in the PGS Points standings, the [b]later the stage from which they will begin their PGC 2026 journey.[/b][/p][p align="start"]The team finishing [b]1st in PGS Points will advance directly to the PGC 2026 Grand Finals[/b]. The [b]2nd-place team will enter at Survival Stage Day 1[/b], while the teams finishing [b]3rd through 8th will begin their journey in the Qualifying Stage[/b].[/p][p align="start"]This means Circuit 4 is about more than simply breaking into the Top 8. For teams already inside the qualification zone, the battle will continue until the very end as they fight for a higher PGS Points ranking and a more advantageous PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]240 PGS Points Are Still Up for Grabs[/b][/p][p align="start"]In both [b]PGS 10 and PGS 11[/b], the winner will earn [b]60 PGS Points[/b], with points awarded down through 16th place.[/p][p align="start"]At the Circuit Final, [b]PGS 12, the points will be doubled[/b]. The winner will earn 120 points, with 96 points going to second place, and double the PGS 10 and PGS 11 point values applied throughout the standings.[/p][p align="start"]That means the maximum number of points a single team can earn in Circuit 4 is:[/p][p align="start"][b]60 points (PGS 10 1st) + 60 points (PGS 11 1st) + 120 points (PGS 12 1st) = 240 points.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Considering the current gaps both inside and outside the PGC qualification zone, the three remaining tournaments leave plenty of room for the final standings to change.[/p][p align="start"]For teams outside the Top 8, Circuit 4 represents one final opportunity to make their move. For those already inside, it will be the final test to defend their position and secure a higher PGC seed.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261012/lwSlSIQk.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: block; float: none; margin: 5px auto; vertical-align: top;"][/img][/p][h2][b]PGS 10 Groups[/b][/h2][p align="start"]And it all begins with [b]PGS 10[/b].[/p][p align="start"]The Group Stage groups have been confirmed for the 24 teams competing in PGS 10. The teams have been divided into Groups A, B, and C through a [b]snake seeding format based on the final results of PGS 9.[/b][/p][p align="start"]PGS 9 winner Gen.G Esports has been placed in Group A, second-place T1 in Group B, and third-place Falcons in Group C. From there, the direction of placement alternates according to the PGS 9 standings, distributing all 24 teams across the three groups.[/p][list][*][p][b]Group A:[/b] Gen.G Esports, Made in Thailand, Virtus.pro, TEAM LIQUID, DN SOOPers, Sharper Esports, Team Vitality, Natus Vincere[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group B:[/b] T1, Alpha Gaming, Team Flash, eArena, Petrichor Road, FULL SENSE, TYLOO, JD Gaming[/p][/*][*][p][b]Group C:[/b] Falcons, Geekay Esports, Anyone’s Legend, 17Gaming, FOUR ANGRY MEN, Twisted Minds, 09(Team Nemesis at PGS 9), Godlike[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=""][tr][td][p align="start"][b]\[Updated: October 12][/b][/p][p align="start"]Following GAM The Expendables’ withdrawal from PGS Circuit 4, Team Flash has been selected as the replacement team based on its placement in PVS Phase 1, in accordance with the existing team qualification criteria.[/p][p align="start"][i]※ Further updates will be provided if there are any changes to the tournament.[/i][/p][/td][/tr][/table][/*][/list][h2][b]The Final Step to PGC[/b][/h2][p align="start"]The 2026 PUBG Global Series journey that began with PGS 1 now has just three tournaments remaining.[/p][p align="start"]There is still everything to play for after Circuit 3. With 60 points available at each of PGS 10 and PGS 11, followed by 120 points at PGS 12, [b]a total of 240 points remain on the table—and a single strong finish could reshape the race to PGC.[/b][/p][p align="start"]Which teams will finish inside the final Top 8 and earn their place at PGC 2026? And which team will rise to the very top of the standings to secure a direct seed to the [b]PGC Grand Finals[/b]?[/p][p align="start"]The final competition of the [b]2026 PUBG Global Series[/b] is about to begin.[/p][p align="start"][b]Tune in and cheer on your favorite teams as they make their final push toward PGC 2026![/b][/p]

title: Virtus.pro and Team Falcons crowned PEC & PAS Finals 2 Champions!
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p]Following an exciting 3 days of action last weekend at the PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall and PUBG Americas Series 2, Virtus.pro and Team Falcons were crowned as the Finals 2 Champions! [/p][p align="start"]Both teams finished the weekend with commanding leads over the rest of the pack. The weekend particularly represented a good return to form for Virtus.pro, who convincingly made up for their 13th place position in Finals 1 with a truly dominant performance in Finals 2 to sweep the lobby. In PAS, Team Falcons’ back-to-back 1st place in Finals 1 and Finals 2 is proof that the superstar squad has fully adapted to the 2026 competitive environment, and we’re excited to see if they can continue their momentum into PGS and PGC on the global stage later this year.[/p][p align="start"]
[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/oMk4NttG.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; min-width: 10px; vertical-align: bottom; border-width: medium; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; text-align: center; width: 1211px; height: 674.379px;"][/img]

[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/eWjV9ecJ.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; min-width: 10px; vertical-align: bottom; border-width: medium; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; text-align: center; width: 1216px; height: 680.31px;"][/img][/p][p align="start"]
[/p][p align="start"]As always, regional PUBG Esports play has a large bearing on which teams can qualify to PGC, through those all-important PGC Points. A number of teams have already qualified directly to PGC through strong regional performances at PEC and PAS.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]Qualified to PGC [/b](through PGC Points earned at regional play):[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p align="center"][b]EMEA[/b][/p][/td][td][p align="center"][b]Americas[/b][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Virtus.pro[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Falcons[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Natus Vincere[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Liquid[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]09[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Godlike[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Twisted Minds[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Circle Nine[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p align="start"]
[/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/pnb6gkk2.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; min-width: 10px; vertical-align: bottom; border-width: medium; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; text-align: center; width: 1170px; height: 655.654px;"][/img][/b][/p][p align="start"][b][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20261007/Joqu7rLy.png" style="border-style: none; max-width: 100%; position: relative; display: inline-block; float: none; margin-left: 5px; margin-right: 5px; min-width: 10px; vertical-align: bottom; border-width: medium; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; text-align: center; width: 1180px; height: 660.395px;"][/img][/b][/p][p align="start"]
[/p][p align="start"]Of course, many of the teams listed above also have a strong possibility of also qualifying to PGC through a good performance at the upcoming PUBG Global Series Circuit 4. If, for example, Viruts.pro puts on a strong performance at the next PGS (and qualifies as a result), their original PGC qualification slot that they earned at PEC will then be redistributed to the next best team from their region’s PGC Points leaderboard. With Virtus.pro and Team Falcons already high in the PGS points table, this means we have a strong chance of seeing [b]Acend Club[/b] and [b]Copenhagen Wolves[/b] (and others) possibly qualify to PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"]As PGC 2026 takes place in Türkiye, there will also be a host region seed for a Turkish team. Stay tuned for more details![/p][p align="start"]If you want to find out who ultimately qualifies to PGC 2026, be sure to tune in to the upcoming PUBG Global Series tournaments![/p][p align="start"]

[b]PUBG Global Series 10: [/b]October 14 - 18[/p][p align="start"][b]PUBG Global Series 11: [/b]October 22 - 25[/p][p align="start"][b]PUBG Global Series 12: [/b]October 29 - November 1[/p][p align="start"][b]PUBG Global Championship 2026: [/b]December 1 - 13[/p]

title: PAS2 Finals 2 Day 3 is LIVE!!
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p]After an exciting weekend of qualifications (and non-qualifications) at last week’s Playoffs 2, it’s now almost time to crown our second (of two) PUBG Americas Series 2 Champions! [/p][p][/p][p]With wins in Finals 1 and 2 of PAS1 respectively, Team Falcons and Team Liquid are the teams to beat. Will their throne(s) be usurped?[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s your look at the lobby:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/4930ebf7775c377fa4170a0da9c4b4f4e79e9e32.png"][/img][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td][p align="center"]+55 e-Sports[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]BILU[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Circle Nine[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Copenhagen Wolves[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]DUEL[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Earthworms[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Godlike[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]NO ORG[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]NO WAY[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Per Diem Withholders[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]PEST Control[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]ROC Esports[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Team Falcons[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team FATE[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Liquid[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]TOYO[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]The PAS2 Finals are all about consistency. We play the classic SUPER format: three match days, and whoever has the most amount of combined kill points and placement points at the end of 15 matches will become the first PAS2 Champion, claiming vital PGC Points in the process! [/p][p][/p][h2]PGC Points[/h2][p]Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PAS2 is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! With 32 teams competing and over $1,500,000 of prize pool on the line (not to mention bragging rights of being the best PUBG team in the world), it’s already shaping up to be a dramatic event. Make sure to tune in to the PAS2 Finals to find out who will secure their tickets to the event![/p][p][/p][h2]Drops[/h2][p]Even if a PAS2 tournament title isn’t in your future, you can still tune in and earn Drops by watching the official broadcast live on Twitch and Kick! [p]After an exciting weekend of qualifications (and non-qualifications) at last week’s Playoffs 2, it’s now almost time to crown our second (of two) PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall Champions! [/p][p][/p][p]Here’s your look at the lobby:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/c6fe8069667e79d573ffa73a3d11a3f0da76436b.png"][/img][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td][p align="center"]09[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]ACEND Club[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Aogiri Tree[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Bushido[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Joga Bonito[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Natus Vincere[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]NewGate[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]noslack[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]PGG[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]S2G Esports[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]S8UL[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Vitality[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Twisted Minds[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Virtus.Pro[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Vis[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]WINside[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]The PEC Finals are all about consistency. We play the classic SUPER format: three match days, and whoever has the most amount of combined kill points and placement points at the end of 15 matches will become the first PEC: Fall Champion![/p][p][/p][h2]PGC Points[/h2][p][/p][p]Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PEC: Fall is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! With 32 teams competing and over $1,500,000 of prize pool on the line (not to mention bragging rights of being the best PUBG team in the world), it’s already shaping up to be a dramatic event. Make sure to tune in to the PEC: Finals to find out who will secure their tickets to the event![/p][p]
[/p][h2]PGC Host Wildcard[/h2][p][/p][p]With PGC taking place in Türkiye, one team for the Türkiye region will also be selected to represent their nation as the host team - seeded directly into the Grand Finals in Istanbul from December 11 - 13. The team will be selected based on performances throughout the year and other criteria - so a strong performance in regional tournaments like PEC could be critical. [/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, if a Turkish team qualifies for PGC via PGC Points, they will automatically receive the wildcard slot. The PGC Points slot will then be assigned to the next best ranked EMEA team in the PGC Points standings. If more than one Turkish team qualify for PGC via PGC Points directly, the top-ranked team will receive the Host Team Wildcard.[/p][p]

title: PAS2 Finals 1 Day 3 is LIVE!!
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p]After an exciting weekend of qualifications (and non-qualifications) at last week’s Playoffs 1, it’s now almost time to crown our first (of two) PUBG Americas Series 2 Champions!
[/p][p]With wins in Finals 1 and 2 of PAS1 respectively, Team Falcons and Team Liquid are the teams to beat. Will their throne(s) be usurped?[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s your look at the lobby:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/1454202cd9cd3fdc4b5909f7c98d3b97f829c89a.png"][/img][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td][p align="center"]ROC Esports[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Circle Nine[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Falcons[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Liquid[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]DUEL[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Copenhagen Wolves[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]TOYO[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]PEST Control[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]GodLike[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]+55 Esports[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Per Diem Withholders[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]ARC e-Sports[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]NO WAY[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]NO ORG[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Last Minute Roster[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Chupinsky[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]The PAS2 Finals are all about consistency. We play the classic SUPER format: three match days, and whoever has the most amount of combined kill points and placement points at the end of 15 matches will become the first PAS2 Champion, claiming vital PGC Points in the process! [/p][p][/p][h2]PGC Points[/h2][p]Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PAS2 is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! With 32 teams competing and over $1,500,000 of prize pool on the line (not to mention bragging rights of being the best PUBG team in the world), it’s already shaping up to be a dramatic event. Make sure to tune in to the PAS2 Finals to find out who will secure their tickets to the event![/p][p][/p][h2]Drops[/h2][p]Even if a PAS2 tournament title isn’t in your future, you can still tune in and earn Drops by watching the official broadcast live on Twitch and Kick! Each day this weekend there’s a new Drop up for grabs - reach 120 minutes of cumulative watch time on a PAS (or PEC, or both!) broadcast on any given day to unlock that day’s drop.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, there will be G-Coin giveaways throughout the broadcast. Check the hints shared on our social media channels during the broadcast to uncover the codes!
[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td rowspan="3"][p]PAS & PEC Finals 1[/p][/td][td][p] Sep 18, 2026[/p][p][i]How to unlock: watch a PEC or PAS stream for 120 minutes[/i][/p][p]PEC: from 18:00 CEST[/p][p]PAS: from 4pm PDT / 7pm EDT[/p][p]
[/p][/td][td][p]THE ORIGINAL IS BACK T-Shirt[/p][/td][td][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//27971017/650c80e1608ff15361aa29bd8febbd3290282599.png" style="border: none; -webkit-user-drag: none; display: block; max-width: 100%;"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p] Sep 19, 2026[/p][/td][td][p]Peculiar Greeting[/p][/td][td][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//27971017/4d51d8648002ef6c25ba497a3af12c52c5f31aa3.png" style="border: none; -webkit-user-drag: none; display: block; max-width: 100%;"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p] Sep 20, 2026[/p][/td][td][p]PUBG Varsity Jacket[/p][/td][td][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//27971017/c7d44ca643f73aeca9770e4c8ac3ac1a6f0b5a53.png" style="border: none; -webkit-user-drag: none; display: block; max-width: 100%;"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p]
And in case you missed it: we had originally planned to also run drops during last weekend’s Playoffs broadcasts, but due to technical issues they were instead moved to the second Finals weekend (Oct 2 - 4). They’ll be available alongside the drops we originally planned, so be extra sure to tune in then for a weekend of double Drops. Mark your calendar![/p]

title: PEC: Fall Finals 1 Day 3 is LIVE!!
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p]After an exciting weekend of qualifications (and non-qualifications) at last week’s Playoffs 1, it’s now almost time to crown our first (of two) PUBG EMEA Championship: Fall Champions!
[/p][p]Will reigning champions Virtus.pro and NAVI retain their tournament title, or will a new challenger usurp them? I guess you’ll just have to find out this weekend…[/p][p][/p][p]Here’s your look at the lobby:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/c7cb33a32aaefd63dbc4e35e0a29a7f21e9ce1b0.png"][/img][/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td][p align="center"]S8UL[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]09[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Vitality[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]S2G Esports[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]ACEND Club[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]PGG[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Joga Bonito[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]noslack[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Virtus.pro[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Everlong[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Bushido Wildcats[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Big John[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Twisted Minds[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Vis[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Natus Vincere[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Kazakhstan[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]The PEC Finals are all about consistency. We play the classic SUPER format: three match days, and whoever has the most amount of combined kill points and placement points at the end of 15 matches will become the first PEC: Fall Champion![/p][p][/p][h2]PGC Points[/h2][p][/p][p]Finals 1 & Finals 2 of PEC: Fall is the final chance for teams to earn PGC Points, which they will use to qualify to the PUBG Global Championship (PGC) 2026, in Istanbul, Türkiye! With 32 teams competing and over $1,500,000 of prize pool on the line (not to mention bragging rights of being the best PUBG team in the world), it’s already shaping up to be a dramatic event. Make sure to tune in to the PEC: Finals to find out who will secure their tickets to the event![/p][p]
[/p][h2]PGC Host Wildcard[/h2][p][/p][p]With PGC taking place in Türkiye, one team for the Türkiye region will also be selected to represent their nation as the host team - seeded directly into the Grand Finals in Istanbul from December 11 - 13. The team will be selected based on performances throughout the year and other criteria - so a strong performance in regional tournaments like PEC could be critical. [/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, if a Turkish team qualifies for PGC via PGC Points, they will automatically receive the wildcard slot. The PGC Points slot will then be assigned to the next best ranked EMEA team in the PGC Points standings. If more than one Turkish team qualify for PGC via PGC Points directly, the top-ranked team will receive the Host Team Wildcard.[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Drops[/h2][p][/p][p]Even if a PEC: Fall tournament title or ticket to Istanbul isn’t in your future, you can still tune in and earn Drops by watching the broadcast live on Twitch and Kick! Each day this weekend there’s a new Drop up for grabs - reach 120 minutes of cumulative watch time on a PEC (or PAS, or both!) broadcast on any given day to unlock that day’s drop.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, there will be G-Coin giveaways throughout the broadcast. Check the hints shared on our social media channels during the broadcast to uncover the codes!
 [/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td rowspan="3"][p]PAS & PEC Finals 1[/p][/td][td][p] Sep 18, 2026[/p][p][i]How to unlock: watch a PEC or PAS stream for 120 minutes[/i][/p][p][/p][p]PEC: from 18:00 CEST[/p][p]PAS: from 4pm PDT / 7pm EDT[/p][p]
[/p][/td][td][p]THE ORIGINAL IS BACK T-Shirt[/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/650c80e1608ff15361aa29bd8febbd3290282599.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p] Sep 19, 2026[/p][/td][td][p]Peculiar Greeting[/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/4d51d8648002ef6c25ba497a3af12c52c5f31aa3.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p] Sep 20, 2026[/p][/td][td][p]PUBG Varsity Jacket[/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/c7d44ca643f73aeca9770e4c8ac3ac1a6f0b5a53.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][/p][p]And in case you missed it: we had originally planned to also run drops during last weekend’s Playoffs broadcasts, but due to technical issues they were instead moved to the second Finals weekend (Oct 2 - 4). They’ll be available alongside the drops we originally planned, so be extra sure to tune in then for a weekend of double Drops. Mark your calendar! [/p]

title: Drop In: PUBG College Royale Returns for the Fall 2026 Season!
author: JBowlerr
contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/71227d56bb298a5e4218863b51d209c2e615cf2e.png"][/img]College PUBG competitors, get your squads ready—[b]PlayVS and KRAFTON are teaming up once again to bring back PUBG College Royale for the Fall 2026 season![/b][/p][p]This free-to-compete event is open to all college students in the U.S. and Canada. [u][url="https://pcl.gg/pages/pubg-college-royale"]Sign up today before the first Qualifier on October 25[/url][/u]. [/p][p]Below is everything you need to know about the upcoming season and how to get involved.[/p][h3][b]What’s at Stake?[/b][/h3][p]We’re leveling up the rewards this season! Top-placing teams will compete for a share of [b]$15,000 in scholarship awards[/b], and on top of that, participants will have the opportunity to earn [b]G-COIN, in-game items, and more[/b] just for competing![/p][h3][b]Tournament Format[/b][/h3][p]The tournament structure is designed to give teams multiple opportunities to stack up points and secure a spot in the championship:[/p][list][*][p][b]Three Open Qualifiers:[/b] Teams will compete across three separate open qualifier events. Each Open Qualifier consists of a 5-match series.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Cumulative Leaderboard:[/b] Teams earn points based on their placement and performance in each Open Qualifier. Results are tracked on a leaderboard where points accumulate across all three opens.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Top 16 Reach the Finals:[/b] The top 16 teams on the leaderboard will advance to the PUBG College Royale Finals. There, they will battle it out across 5 final matches live on stream to be crowned the Fall 2026 Champions and claim their share of the $15k prize pool![/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Fall 2026 Schedule[/b][/h3][p]Mark your calendars![/p][list][*][p][b]Registration Opens:[/b] Thursday, September 17[/p][/*][*][p][b]Open #1:[/b] Sunday, October 25[/p][list][*][p]Register for free [u][url="https://esports.pcl.gg/seasons/f1860374-6d61-4e93-a46b-037db17aae58"]HERE[/url][/u] [/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Open #2:[/b] Sunday, November 1[/p][list][*][p]Register for free [u][url="https://esports.pcl.gg/seasons/a6310e72-8498-4bdd-87cc-1370dcd6dfee"]HERE[/url][/u] [/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Open #3:[/b] Sunday, November 8[/p][list][*][p]Regiser for free [u][url="https://esports.pcl.gg/seasons/8461148c-f811-41ce-b551-44cefb86072b"]HERE[/url][/u] [/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Finals (Live Streamed):[/b] Sunday, November 22[/p][/*][/list][p]Matches get underway at [b]3:00 PM ET / 12:00 PM PT[/b] each day.[/p][h3][b]Ready to Drop In?[/b][/h3][p]Registration is officially [b]OPEN[/b]! Assemble your roster, lock in your strategies, and prepare to represent your school.[/p][p]For full eligibility details, rulebooks, and registration links, visit [url="https://pcl.gg/pages/pubg-college-royale"]pcl.gg/pages/pubg-college-royale[/url][/p]

title: PGS 9: How Did Gen.G Become a Top Team?
author: Eoin
contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/2f450a8e142189ec53132a1580fa5f255a2a0e1c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]In the wake of Gen.G’s dramatic PGS 9 tournament win, we enlisted the help of PUBG expert reporter Jisooboy to analyse what precisely led to their tournament win! Here’s what they had to say:[/i][/p][p][/p][p align="start"]When people think of the greatest organizations in PUBG Esports, a few teams naturally come to mind. Among them is Gen.G Esports, the 2019 PGC champion and a storied organization that has represented PUBG Esports for years. Yet after winning PGC 2019, Gen.G struggled to produce meaningful results. Following a third-place finish at PGI.S 2021, the team failed to win a single title across the PCS ASIA series or any subsequent PGC. Despite multiple rebuilds year after year, its only notable result was a runner-up finish at EWC 2025. Gen.G clearly needed a change.[/p][p align="start"]Perhaps that is why Gen.G entered this year with a different level of ambition. The team signed seoul Cho Gi-yeol and Salute Woo Je-hyeon, both members of the PGC 2023 championship roster, as well as diyy Daniel Noh Noh Eun-woo, who had delivered standout performances for Al Qadsiah. In particular, seoul and Salute had been regarded as one of Korea’s strongest duos, sending expectations among PUBG Esports fans sky-high.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]But the result of that major rebuild was disastrous. Gen.G finished only fourth in the domestic PWS, while its chances of qualifying for PGC began to fade. The team missed the Finals four times—at PGS 1, 2, 5, and 7 in 2026—and across 123 PGS matches recorded just seven Chicken Dinners, 3.49 kills per match, and 789 average damage per match. The numbers did not lie. It would not have been an exaggeration to call Gen.G one of the weakest Partner Teams competing in PGS.[/p][p align="start"]Sure enough, Gen.G opened the first PGS Circuit, Circuit 1, by missing the Finals three times in a row. Gen.G was not alone—many teams that had undergone major rebuilds were also struggling to find their footing—but three consecutive Finals misses in Circuit 1 was still a shocking result.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]As a Global Partner Team, Gen.G had the advantage of guaranteed participation in the PGS Circuit and more opportunities to accumulate PGS Points. Even so, it was pushed aside by established Partner Teams and strong regional qualifiers, failing not only to break into the PGS top eight but even falling into the bottom tier of the standings. Considering Gen.G’s history on the international stage, it was a deeply disappointing run.[/p][p align="start"]The crisis continued in PGS Circuit 2. Gen.G appeared to be turning things around with a sixth-place finish at PGS 4, only to finish 23rd at PGS 5 and miss the Finals once again. The swings could hardly have been more extreme. The team returned to the Finals at PGS 6, but finished just 13th overall. Without a dramatic turnaround in Circuit 3, direct qualification to PGC was becoming almost impossible to imagine.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]In my view, there were two main reasons for Gen.G’s struggles. First, the team had not had enough time to build chemistry. Second, communication was not yet smooth. Individual skill was never the issue. Every player already had extensive international experience and an impressive career behind them.[/p][p align="start"]Meanwhile, the 2026 PUBG Esports season began with PGS. Many teams had rebuilt their rosters in January 2026, and because the opening competition was an international event rather than a domestic league, the level of opposition was extremely high. In roughly two months, teams had to establish their approach to macro play, understand each new teammate’s tendencies, sharpen the precision of information sharing, and raise the level of their teamplay in fights.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]For newly signed diyy in particular, the language barrier made it difficult to exchange information and coordinate opinions smoothly with his teammates. It was something that had surfaced across tournaments, scrims, personal streams, and Ranked play, and it did not look like an issue that could be solved overnight. Beyond the differences in how overseas and Korean players make comms, it is difficult to completely learn every in-game callout, terrain reference, and piece of slang in just a few months. A building called ‘Palgakjeong’ in Korea, for example, may be called ‘Wizard Tower’ overseas. Depending on the map, there can be hundreds of callouts like these.[/p][p align="start"]As these issues accumulated, comms mistakes became more frequent and information took longer to relay, inevitably leading to repeated teamkills and in-game errors. While Gen.G worked through that process, rival teams steadily built their own careers and collected prize money. Gen.G could do little but watch from the sidelines.[/p][p align="start"]After enduring all of those difficulties, signs of change finally began to appear for Gen.G in PGS Circuit 3. The team finished only 11th overall at PGS 8, but many of the issues that had been repeatedly pointed out were beginning to improve. The result itself was not strong, yet the quality of Gen.G’s play had changed significantly. Cleaner comms, pre-planned setups, and more precise approaches began to take shape. As the team reorganized its positions and role order, both survival time and the rate at which it secured Placement Points began to rise.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]PGS 8 Finals DAY 1 MATCH 1 — Erangel[/b][/p][p align="start"]Looking at Gen.G’s Chicken Dinner in Finals DAY 1 MATCH 1 on Erangel, the team focused on keeping all four players alive by denying routes other teams could use and gathering information before winning the decisive fight. The closing sequence still showed some instability. Gen.G held the stronger position, but when information about each player’s situation was not shared quickly enough, dangerous moments like this could still occur. Even so, the match helped Gen.G sharpen its form as the tournament progressed.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]PGS 8 Finals DAY 2 MATCH 2 — Erangel[/b][/p][p align="start"]The second highlight was how well the revised roles worked in tournament play. Gen.G’s typical losing pattern had often looked like this: ① Salute looks for an angle to hunt another team → ② if the opponent responds well or Gen.G cannot execute quickly as a team, Salute is neutralized → ③ BeaN and diyy try to help, only to get knocked in succession or draw a third party → ④ Seoul makes a big play at the end, but the team still goes down soon after.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]Gen.G’s Typical Losing Pattern[/b][/p][p align="start"]Over time, however, the revised positioning and order changed that pattern. When Gen.G needed to look for a third-party angle or take the initiative and eliminate an opponent first, Seoul moved to the front, combining detailed reads of the situation with smooth, persistent pressure. BeaN and diyy acted as the glue in the middle, while Salute surveyed the wider battlefield from the backline and took responsibility for the final calls. The new structure began to pay off.[/p][p align="start"]The role changes improved Gen.G’s overall survival time and Placement Point output. At the PGS 6 Grand Finals, Gen.G averaged only 1.4 Placement Points per match; by the PGS 9 Finals, that figure had risen to 3.9. The team’s average survival time also increased from 20 minutes 53 seconds to 22 minutes 38 seconds. Salute’s combat numbers, which had dipped somewhat after taking on the main IGL role, also began to recover. Team average damage jumped sharply from 672 to 980.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]In a way, perhaps every problem Gen.G had faced ultimately came down to time. Salute, for example, moved from an attacking role into responsibility for the team’s calls, giving him far more to process and manage and preventing him from playing at his best. BeaN, serving as the glue of the team, needed above all to become a stable, mistake-free presence with the ability to survive tenaciously—and it took time to fully develop that role. Seoul was always elite statistically, but those numbers had largely been individual. There were moments when he needed to step forward before the team began to collapse. diyy, meanwhile, needed to reshape the entire style of play he had been accustomed to.[/p][p align="start"]Gen.G’s strengths are now clear. The team had always built good scenarios for attacking opponents, but it lacked the finishing power and clearly defined roles needed to complete them. Now Seoul and Salute, two of the best players in the world, have fully settled into their respective roles, while BeaN’s survival instincts—honed over years in the PUBG scene—have matured into a major strength. Even diyy, who had repeatedly made costly mistakes, played the biggest role in delivering Gen.G the championship in the final match of the PGS 9 FINAL.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b][u][url="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Vq26m4PdyXA?si=j5vAsO-zk7lpb5Yi"]Salute’s Read of the Situation + Seoul’s Composed Finish[/url][/u][/b][/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b][u][url="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/XvY-rbRERz0"]BeaN’s Brilliant Placement Defense[/url][/u][/b][/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b][u][url="https://www.youtube.com/shorts/mrvSetaK3dc"]diyy’s Winning Play for the Championship[/url][/u][/b][/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Of course, while this column was being written, it was announced that diyy had ended his contract and transferred to Team Liquid on August 25, 2026. Gen.G then announced another rebuild by signing taemin Kang Tae-min on August 27, 2026, one of the key players from the PGC 2019 championship roster. There is a chance that the gaps discussed above could emerge once again, but every player on Gen.G has the experience and skill to fill them, so there may be little reason for serious concern.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b]Closing[/b][/p][p align="start"]994 days.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]That is how long Korean PUBG Esports had gone quiet on the international stage since its PGC 2023 championship. Gen.G, too, had to endure repeated failures and rebuilds while searching for a way back to the top. The players changed roles, learned to understand one another’s play, and endured countless rounds of trial and error before finally becoming one complete team. In the end, what made Gen.G a top team again was not a single signing or one special strategy. It was the time required to understand one another, the experience gained by enduring failure, and the determination of players who refused to give up until the very end.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]After quietly enduring failure after failure, Gen.G finally lifted an international trophy. In doing so, one of PUBG Esports’ most storied organizations proved itself once again: a great team is not simply made—it is completed only after surviving countless failures. We remember all the losses they endured in order to become stronger. And those memories will only make Gen.G stronger still.[/p][p align="start"]- Jisooboy[/p]

title: PUBG GLOBAL SERIES 9 GRAND FINALS DAY 3 IS LIVE!
author: JBowlerr
contents:
[p]Hello, PUBG Esports Fans!

PGS Circuit 3 is about to conclude with an explosive four days of PUBG esports action at [b]PGS 9[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]As the Circuit Final approaches, here’s what you need to know about the tournament format, where to watch, drops and more.

[/p][h3][b]Schedule[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][b]Survival Stage[/b]: August 20th[/p][list][*][p]Seeding for PGS 9 is based on teams’ performance in PGS 7 and 8. The Top 8 teams from those tournaments will bypass the Survival Stage and go directly to the Finals. Everyone else will duke it out in the 16-team Survival Stage on Thursday, in a last-chance dash to make it to the ultimate PGS Finals lobby. Only the Top 8 can advance from the Survival Stage![/p][/*][/list][p][b]Grand Finals[/b]: August 21st - 23rd[/p][list][*][p]A  no-holds-barred three day BO15 fight for the PGS Champion title. At the end of PGS 12, the top eight teams in the annual PGS Points standings will qualify directly for PGC 2026.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]For the teams that built an advantage in the first half, Shanghai is where they must defend it. For those chasing from behind, the doubled points create an opportunity to turn the standings around. One strong circuit could reshape the entire PGC race.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Map Pool and Order[/h2][p align="start"]Circuit 3 will be played across Erangel, Miramar, Taego, and Rondo.[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,,,"][tr][th][p]Stage[/p][p][/p][/th][th][p]Match 1[/p][p][/p][/th][th][p]Match 2[/p][p][/p][/th][th][p]Match 3[/p][p][/p][/th][th][p]Match 4[/p][p][/p][/th][th][p]Match 5[/p][p][/p][/th][/tr][tr][td][p]Group Stage [/p][/td][td][p]Erangel [/p][/td][td][p]Miramar [/p][/td][td][p]Taego [/p][/td][td][p]— [/p][/td][td][p]— [/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Winners / Survival / Final Day 1 / Grand Finals Days 1 & 3 [/p][/td][td][p]Erangel [/p][/td][td][p]Miramar [/p][/td][td][p]Taego [/p][/td][td][p]Rondo [/p][/td][td][p]Erangel [/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Final Day 2 / Grand Finals Day 2 [/p][/td][td][p]Taego [/p][/td][td][p]Erangel [/p][/td][td][p]Rondo [/p][/td][td][p]Miramar [/p][/td][td][p]Taego [/p][/td][/tr][/table][p align="start"]The Group Stage repeats the same Erangel → Miramar → Taego order across all three group matchups for Matches 1 through 9.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Prize Pool[/h2][p align="start"]The total prize pool for Circuit 3 is $500,000, distributed across the three series.[/p][list][*][p]PGS 7: $100,000 — $30,000 for the champion[/p][/*][*][p]PGS 8: $100,000 — $30,000 for the champion[/p][/*][*][p]PGS 9: $300,000 — $100,000 for the champion[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]Placement prizes will be awarded to the top eight teams in PGS 7 and PGS 8, and to all 16 Grand Finalists in PGS 9. Each series also features separate match-win and MVP prizes.[/p][p align="start"]Across four circuits and 12 series, the total prize pool for the 2026 PGS season is $2,000,000.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]How to Watch[/h2][p align="start"]All PGS 7–9 matches will be broadcast live on official PUBG Esports channels.[/p][p align="start"]Matches begin at 10:00 UTC daily, except for the PGS 7 Group Stage on August 5, which begins at 05:00 UTC.[/p][p align="start"]Detailed broadcast channels and viewing links will be announced separately.[/p][p align="start"]A new city, double the points, and 24 teams fighting for their place at PGC 2026. Circuit 3 will set the direction for the second half of the 2026 season.[/p][p align="start"]See you in Shanghai on August 5![/p]
